question: What did the Solar Orbiter spacecraft reveal in 2025 about the Sun's south pole?
text:
Solar Orbiter captured the first clear images of the Sun’s south pole in March 2025. Its magnetic maps revealed **patches of both north and south magnetic polarity** side by side, rather than one dominant polarity. ESA released the images on June 11, 2025. ([esa.int](https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Solar_Orbiter/Solar_Orbiter_gets_world-first_views_of_the_Sun_s_poles?utm_source=openai))

That patchwork is characteristic of solar maximum, the active phase of the Sun’s roughly 11-year cycle when its global magnetic field reverses. ([esa.int](https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Solar_Orbiter/Solar_Orbiter_gets_world-first_views_of_the_Sun_s_poles?utm_source=openai))
